room.title: Real Estate and Property Management
room.description: How an agent and a property manager keep a sale campaign and a busy rent roll in view — buyers, vendor reports, maintenance quotes and owner approvals on one surface instead of a CRM, a PMS and a notebook.

desks.title: 14 Banksia Crescent — auction campaign, week 3
desks.description: A four-week auction campaign heading into its last stretch: every buyer and where they're at, the vendor report, and the reserve conversation that has to happen before auction day.
desks.brief:
## 14 Banksia Crescent — auction campaign

**Property** 4 bed, 2 bath family home on 680 m² — renovated kitchen, single garage, backs onto bushland
**Vendors** Helen and Doug · downsizing, already bought, settlement flexible
**Auction** on site @+9d · **Price guide** $1.05m–$1.15m, the estimate in the agency agreement
**Vendors' expectation** $1.2m

### Campaign so far (week 3 of 4)
- 3 open homes, 41 groups through, 6 private inspections
- 11 active buyers, 6 with finance approved
- 3 contracts requested, 1 building and pest inspection done

### The problem to solve
Price feedback from nine buyers averages $1.06m and tops out at $1.12m. Helen and Doug's number is $1.2m. **The reserve conversation is @+5d**, and it has to be built on this table, not on hope.

callout.title: Reserve conversation @+5d
callout.body: Buyer feedback averages $1.06m, the strongest is $1.12m, and Helen and Doug want $1.2m. Go in with the buyer table, the three contract requests and a recommended reserve of $1.1m.

rows.next: Their solicitor is reviewing the contract
Yard too much work — townhouse list
Comparing with a house two streets away
Booked into the next open home @+2d

children.label: Chase the building and pest result
Pre-auction offer from Anika and Raj?
Who can pay the deposit on the day?

blocks.p: Helen and Doug — here's where the campaign stands, with the auction @+9d.

ul: 41 groups through three open homes, plus 6 private inspections
11 active buyers; 3 have asked for the contract
Anika and Raj have had a building and pest inspection done

blocks.h4: What buyers are saying about price

blocks.p: Nine buyers have given price feedback. It ranges from $930k to $1.12m and averages $1.06m. The two strongest, both at $1.12m, have finance approved.
A reserve of **$1.1m**. It sits just under what the two strongest buyers have told us, which gives us a real chance of two bidders on the day. We'll talk through your $1.2m when we meet @+5d.

blocks.quote: Price feedback isn't an offer. Three contract requests by week 3 is the stronger signal.

notes.title: Open home follow-ups
notes.body:
From the last open home (14 groups):

- Jack and Ellie: loved the kitchen, worried about the retaining wall — their builder comes through @+4d
- Diego: says the yard is too much work; added to the townhouse list
- Samira: broker meeting @+3d, call her after
- Two groups asked about plans for the bushland behind — check with council before anyone asks again

Call every group back within 24 hours, before 10am.

stickies.title: Before the vendor meeting
stickies.body:
Print the buyer table
Comparable sales, last 6 months
Reserve to recommend: $1.1m

stickies.title: Auction admin
stickies.body:
Bidder registration forms and the auctioneer's run sheet to the office @+7d.
Reserve to the auctioneer in writing before bidding opens.
Deposit on the day: 10%.

desks.title: Rent roll — maintenance queue and owner approvals
desks.description: A property manager's week across a 140-property rent roll: open maintenance jobs, quotes waiting on owners, one urgent repair and the routine inspections coming due.
desks.brief:
## Maintenance queue — owner approvals

**Rent roll** 140 properties · me, plus Jade on leasing and inspections
**Approval limit** up to $500 without asking; above that, the owner approves in writing
**Urgent repairs** straight to the trade, owner told the same day

### On the board this week
- 10 jobs: 8 open, 2 completed · $6,770 quoted
- $4,130 of that is four quotes waiting on owners, each for over a week
- 1 urgent: no hot water at 3/22 Lilly Pilly Lane
- 6 routine inspections due by @+14d; entry notices out for 2

### The pattern to fix
Jobs don't stall with the trades — they stall with owners. A two-line email with photos and one question gets answered from a phone; a PDF quote on its own sits in an inbox. **Every approval request goes out on the template from today.**

callout.title: Urgent: no hot water, owner not answering
callout.body: 3/22 Lilly Pilly Lane — the hot water system failed and the tenant has two young children. Plumber booked @today at 2pm, $1,850 to replace. Two calls to the owner unanswered; photos and quote emailed, follow-up call @+1d.

rows.issue: Switchboard trips when the oven is on
Fence palings down after the storm
Shower recess leaking into the wall

children.label: Photos into the PMS the same day
Re-list at the same rent or +$20?
Rent review letters to owners first

page.title: Owner approval — the email that gets answered

blocks.p: Short enough to answer from a phone. Photos inline, quote attached, one question.

blocks.quote: Hi [owner] — the shower recess at 7 Tuckeroo Road is leaking into the wall cavity (photos below). The plumber's quote to re-seal it and replace the waste is $1,240. OK to go ahead? If I haven't heard by @+3d, I'll text, and I'll call @+5d.

ul: One property, one job, one question — owners answer questions, not updates
The cost of waiting is stated: water in a wall cavity gets dearer every week
Follow-up dates, so the next steps are a text and a call, not another email

ol: Past day 10: note it on the owner's file and raise it at their next review

notes.title: Calls to make today
notes.body:
- Owner of 3/22 Lilly Pilly Lane — third try before the plumber arrives at 2pm; if no answer, text that the photos and quote are in their inbox, and call again @+1d
- Tenant at 41 Corkwood Grove — arrears and the switchboard in the same call, gently
- Roofer: can the Grevillea Way stain and the Melaleuca Drive gutters be one trip? Different owners, same morning
- Jade: entry notices for the four remaining routine inspections

stickies.title: Approval limit
stickies.body: Up to $500: book it. Over $500: owner approves in writing. Urgent: book it, then tell them.

stickies.title: Inspections
stickies.body:
6 due by @+14d
Notices out: 2 of 6
Jade sends the rest @+1d
7 days' written notice each time

images.title: Failed hot water system, Lilly Pilly Lane
images.prompt: Documentary photograph of a failed electric hot water storage cylinder in the cramped outdoor laundry alcove of an older brick block of units: rust streaks running down the plain unbranded white casing, a shallow puddle spreading across the concrete floor, and a plumber's gloved hands kneeling beside an open canvas tool bag holding a shiny new copper fitting. Overcast morning light, close matter-of-fact framing, muted natural colours, the feel of a condition photo taken for an owner.

images.title: Storm-damaged fence, Casuarina Court
images.prompt: Documentary photograph of a suburban Australian backyard the morning after a storm: a weathered grey timber paling fence with a run of palings knocked flat onto wet grass and one rail hanging loose, scattered gum leaves and small branches across the lawn, shallow puddles reflecting a grey sky that is clearing to soft light, a plain corrugated steel fence in the background. Wide eye-level framing, honest condition-report feel, no people.
